title: Phase-coalescing scheduler for asynchronous tensor/pipeline handoffs with NCCL crediting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our multi-GPU prefill+decode path shows suboptimal NCCL overlap and high tail latency for mixed-seqlen traffic. When stage boundaries don't align across the microbatch wave, GPUs idle while waiting for rendezvous or fall back to many small NCCL collectives. This hurts p99 latency and raises per-token GPU costs for medium-length requests.

Goal: Implement a phase-coalescing scheduling layer that groups adjacent short/partial prefill windows across tensor/pipeline stages into creditized NCCL windows and enables asynchronous handoffs with kernel hints. The scheduler should: (1) reduce rendezvous stalls by opportunistically merging short-stage handoffs, (2) bias kernel selection toward fused attention kernels when handoff latency predicts benefit, and (3) maintain deterministic fallbacks for safety.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change model partitioning logic or implement new NCCL primitives. It focuses on runtime scheduling policies, credit bookkeeping, and telemetry to validate overlap increases.
technical_approach:
1) Introduce a lightweight CreditBucket abstraction per rendezvous point: microbatches contribute credits proportional to token count and deadline slack. CreditBuckets allow merging up to an adaptive time-slice threshold (configurable by policy) to form a single NCCL window.

2) Time-slice coalescer: when a stage signals a short prefill/hand-off (< X ms predicted), the coalescer holds the token wave for up to the bucket slack to await neighboring stage arrivals. If the bucket fills or slack expires, trigger a single NCCL collective covering combined tensors.

3) Async handoff fences: replace strict synchronous stage barriers with low-overhead SHM fences and a best-effort completion callback that permits downstream kernels to start local computation using kernel-hints (e.g., begin fused attention compute for already-available KV shards).

4) Kernel hinting & selection: extend kernel selector to accept a latency_budget estimate from the scheduler. If merged window increases effective throughput but tightens latency, select lower-latency fused attention kernels or lower-precision quantized kernels for that window.

5) Telemetry & safety: emit per-bucket metrics (bucket_fill, held_ms, merged_collective_size, p99_before_after) and a global safety circuit that disables coalescing when error rates or out-of-memory signals increase.

6) Rollout: feature-flagged opt-in on dedicated clusters; AB test against baseline with synthetic mixed-seqlen traces and customer workloads.

Implementation notes: keep CreditBucket lock-free where possible, use atomic ring slots for contributors, and limit memory copies by reusing rendezvous buffers. Unit-level deterministic simulators will validate merging logic before running on hardware labs.
acceptance_criteria: Measurable improvement: >=8% reduction in p99 latency on 8xA100 prefill-decode mixed-seqlen benchmark compared to baseline when coalescing enabled
No regression in median throughput (>95% of baseline QPS) under sustained load
Comprehensive telemetry available in Console: per-bucket metrics and rollout dashboards
Kernel selector honors latency_budget hint; covered by unit and integration tests
Feature gated and can be toggled per-cluster with safe fallback to baseline rendezvous
Documentation: design doc and operator runbook updated with configuration knobs and failure modes
